1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls authorized(), which resolves the account solely from the server-side session's userId and never from client-supplied identifiers, so settings always belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: Challenges are stored per-session (session.identity, session.fixture), but DEMO_MODE (default whenever NODE_ENV !== 'production') hardcodes the same '123456' identity code, '654321' authenticator code and a fixed recovery-code list for every account, so those codes are identical for any user.

3.why: Sign-in deletes only the current session and creates a new one; enabling the authenticator (/api/authenticator/verify) or confirming backups never iterates the sessions map to invalidate the user's other existing sessions, so pre-existing sessions remain valid until idle/absolute timeout.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext (encrypt()/pendingSecret → account.secret) and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes in the backups Map, never in plain text.

5.why: Session IDs, CSRF tokens, TOTP seeds, keys and pepper all use crypto.randomBytes/randomInt, but in the default demo mode the identity code, authenticator code and recovery codes are hardcoded constants rather than CSPRNG output.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used; secrets/codes only live transiently in JS variables and DOM text (and are console.logged in demo mode), which is not persistent browser storage.

7.why: Server-side validation includes emailOK, otpOK, codeOK regexes, a method allow-list ('email'|'phone'), a 10 KB body limit, password length cap, and JSON object type checks; there is no SQL/datastore query to inject into.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted client-side via textContent/replaceChildren, the HTML template interpolates only a server-generated nonce, and a strict nonce-based CSP with base-uri 'none' blocks inline/injected script.

9.why: The application implements no redirect functionality at all (no Location headers, no location assignment), so there is no open-redirect surface, though no explicit allow-list exists either.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: cookieValue()/clearCookie emit 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=...' on all session cookies.

12.why: Server errors are caught and returned as a generic message with no stack traces, and nothing sensitive appears in URLs, but simulatedDelivery() deliberately console.logs the identity OTP, authenticator code and full recovery-code list to the browser console.

13.why: Identity codes and demo fixtures carry expires (10 min) plus a 'used' flag, and recovery codes flip to used-once in the Map; the only gap is validTotp accepting a ±1 step drift window, allowing brief reuse of a TOTP value.

14.why: Separate Failures counters for sign-in, identity, authenticator and recovery lock for 15 minutes after 5 failures, plus a 3-per-15-minutes cap on identity code requests, returning HTTP 429.

15.why: Successful sign-in deletes the old session and issues a brand-new opaque ID and CSRF token, getSession enforces a 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
